title: Introduction to SAT Math and Mathematical Modeling
subtitle: Learn the structure of the Digital SAT Math section and turn real-world language into accurate mathematical models.

isi.content: This meeting introduces the Digital SAT Math section and the central idea of mathematical modeling. A model translates a real situation into an expression, equation, inequality, system, table, or graph that can be analyzed.

items: Translate the important words into mathematics.
Keep units consistent and combine related quantities.
Interpret the result and check whether it is reasonable.

isi.content: The goal is not to memorize every formula immediately. The goal is to build reliable habits that make later Algebra, Advanced Math, Problem-Solving and Data Analysis, Geometry, and Trigonometry questions easier to understand.

The Digital SAT Math section has two modules. Each module contains 22 questions and allows 35 minutes. The second module is adaptive, so performance in the first module affects the difficulty of the second module.

rows: Everyone gets the same set of questions with the same level of difficulty.

The SAT uses adaptive difficulty. Everyone who performs well in Module 1 will receive a set of questions with a higher level of difficulty in Module 2, while those who do not perform well will receive an easier set of questions.
The maximum score a test-taker can achieve depends on whether they are directed to the easier or harder version of Module 2. If placed into the easier Module 2, the maximum score in a section is usually around 620–630, while the harder Module 2 allows for a full score up to 800.

isi.content:
Questions may be multiple-choice or student-produced responses.
Multiple-choice questions provide four choices.
Student-produced response, you enter the numerical answer directly.

Timing matters: 22 questions in 35 minutes in each module is an average of about 1 minute 35 seconds per question. Some questions will take less time, leaving more time for questions that require modeling or multi-step reasoning.

rows: If you find more than one correct answer, enter just one answer.
Enter up to 5 characters for a positive answer.
Enter up to 6 characters (this includes the negative sign) for a negative answer.
If your answer is a mixed number, enter it as an improper fraction or its decimal equivalent.
Only enter numbers, decimal point, slash (fraction), or negative sign.

materi.judul: The four SAT Math content areas

items.title: Algebra
items.content: Linear equations, systems, inequalities, and linear functions.

items.title: Advanced Math
items.content: Nonlinear equations, quadratics, exponentials, circles, and equivalent expressions.

items.title: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis
items.content: Ratios, percentages, rates, probability, statistics, and data interpretation.

items.title: Geometry and Trigonometry
items.content: Lines, angles, triangles, circles, area, volume, and right-triangle relationships.

isi.content: These areas often overlap. For example, a geometry question may require an equation, and a data question may require a percentage model. Strong modeling helps connect the topics.
A variable represents an unknown or changing quantity. A constant is a fixed number. A coefficient is a number that multiplies a variable.
In \(7x+12\), \(x\) is the variable, 7 is the coefficient, and 12 is the constant. This is an expression because it does not contain an equals sign. By contrast, \(7x+12=40\) is an equation.
Define variables with meaning and units when possible. For example, write “Let \(x\) be the number of tickets” rather than only writing “Let \(x\).”

Read comparison phrases from the reference quantity outward.
The phrase “5 less than \(x\)” means \(x-5\), not \(5-x\).

rows: \(x\) is greater than or equal to 20.
\(x\) is less than or equal to 20.

isi.title: Classify which statement belongs to each notation
isi.prompt: Let \(x\) be the number of students. Match each notation with every statement that describes it.
statements: The number of students is equal to 30.
The number of students is more/greater than 30.
The number of students is more than or equal to 30.
The number of students is less than 30.
The number of students is less than or equal to 30.
The number of students is at least/cannot be less than 30.
The number of students is at most/cannot be greater than 30.
The number of students cannot exceed 30.
The maximum number of students is 30.
The minimum number of students is 30.
The exact number of students is 30.
discussion: \(x=30\) means the number is exactly 30, so it matches statements a and k.
\(x<30\) means the number is less than 30, so it matches statement d.
\(x\le30\) means the number is less than or equal to 30. It also means the number is at most 30, cannot exceed 30, and has a maximum of 30, so it matches statements e, g, h, and i.
\(x>30\) means the number is greater than 30, so it matches statement b.
\(x\ge30\) means the number is greater than or equal to 30. It also means the number is at least 30, cannot be less than 30, and has a minimum of 30, so it matches statements c, f, and j.

items: Define the variables: state what each variable measures.
Translate the relationships: watch for words such as “per,” “total,” “twice,” and “at least.”
Combine the relationships: choose an expression, equation, inequality, system, or piecewise model.
Interpret the result: check units, signs, boundaries, and realistic values.

isi.title: Example: a ticket-revenue model
isi.content:
A movie theater charges USD \(12\) for each adult ticket and USD \(8\) for each child ticket. If \(a\) represents the number of adult tickets sold and \(c\) represents the number of child tickets sold, which expression represents the total amount collected?

⤳ Adult tickets cost USD \(12\) and child tickets cost USD \(8\);
⤳ \(a\) is the number of adult tickets and \(c\) is the number of child tickets.

Then,
Adult revenue is \(12a\) and child revenue is \(8c\);
so the total revenue is \(R=12a+8c\)
Units are part of the meaning of a number. A per-unit rate is multiplied by the number of units, while a fixed charge is added separately.
\[\text{Total cost}=(\text{rate})(\text{number of units})+\text{fixed fee}\]

isi.title: Example: convert hours to minutes
isi.content: A phone costs USD \(0.20\) per minute. If it is used for \(h\) hours, then \(h\) hours equals \(60h\) minutes. The cost is \(C=0.20(60h)=12h\) dollars.

isi.title: Example: a piecewise delivery cost
isi.content:
A delivery service charges USD 18 for the first 10 miles and USD 1.40 for each additional mile.

So, for \(0 < d \le 10 \), \(C=18\).
Then, for \(d > 10\), it costs \(d-10\) additional miles are charged $C=18+1.40(d-10)$.
Do not combine hours with minutes, pounds with ounces, or percentages with whole-number amounts without converting to compatible units.

items.title: Inequality
items.content: A limit or range, such as \(x+y\le1000\).

items.title: System
items.content: Several conditions that must hold at the same time.

isi.title: Example: interpret a system
isi.content:
A nutrition create a meal plan using protein bars and smoothies. Each protein bar contains 12 grams of protein and 5 grams of sugar. Each smoothie contains 20 grams of protein and 14 grams of sugar. The plan needs at least 100 grams of protein and no more than 60 grams of sugar. If \(b\) is the number of bars and \(s\) is the number of smoothies, which system models the situation?

The plan must consist at least 100 grams of protein gives \(12b+20s\ge100\),
while no more than 60 grams of sugar gives \(5b+14s\le60\).
“At least” and “no less than” use \(\ge\). “At most,” “no more than,” and “cannot exceed” use \(\le\). The boundary is included in these phrases.

materi.judul: SAT Math tools and checking habits

items: Use Desmos to graph equations and inequalities, find intersections, check zeros and intercepts, evaluate expressions, and test a proposed model.
Use the SAT reference sheet for formulas, but identify what each variable in the formula represents before substituting.
Estimate before calculating. A negative number of people or a cost below zero is usually a sign that the model was misread.
Use answer choices strategically by testing a convenient value when the question asks which expression matches.
Keep an error log: record whether a mistake came from translation, arithmetic, units, or interpretation.

isi.content: A calculator can verify a model, but it cannot repair a sentence that was translated incorrectly.

latihan.question: A movie theater charges USD \(12\) for each adult ticket and USD \(8\) for each child ticket. If \(a\) represents the number of adult tickets sold and \(c\) represents the number of child tickets sold, which expression represents the total amount collected?
discussion: Adult tickets contribute \(12a\) dollars.
Child tickets contribute \(8c\) dollars.
Adding the two revenue sources gives \(12a+8c\), so choice B is correct.

latihan.question: A gym orders cases of water bottles. Each case contains 24 bottles. If the gym orders \(n\) cases, which expression represents the total number of bottles ordered?
discussion: There are 24 bottles in each case.
For \(n\) equal cases, multiply \(24\) by \(n\): \(24n\).
Therefore, choice C is correct.

latihan.question: A parking garage can hold no more than 450 cars. If \(s\) represents the number of small cars and \(l\) represents the number of large cars, which inequality models the situation?
discussion: The total number of cars is \(s+l\).
“No more than 450” means 450 or fewer, so the symbol is \(\le\).
The model is \(s+l\le450\), choice C.

latihan.question: Peanuts are 30% protein by weight, and almonds are 20% protein by weight. If \(p\) pounds of peanuts and \(a\) pounds of almonds provide 50 pounds of protein, which equation models the situation?
discussion: Peanuts contribute \(0.30p\) pounds of protein.
Almonds contribute \(0.20a\) pounds of protein.
The total is 50 pounds, so \(0.30p+0.20a=50\). Choice C is correct.

latihan.question: Each protein bar contains 12 grams of protein and 5 grams of sugar. Each smoothie contains 20 grams of protein and 14 grams of sugar. The plan needs at least 100 grams of protein and no more than 60 grams of sugar. If \(b\) is the number of bars and \(s\) is the number of smoothies, which system models the situation?
discussion: Protein is \(12b+20s\), and “at least 100” gives \(12b+20s\ge100\).
Sugar is \(5b+14s\), and “no more than 60” gives \(5b+14s\le60\).
Together these are choice A.

latihan.question: Orange juice contains 15% sugar and mango juice contains 10% sugar. If \(o\) pounds of orange juice and \(m\) pounds of mango juice provide 18 pounds of sugar, which equation models the situation?
discussion: The sugar from orange juice is \(0.15o\) pounds.
The sugar from mango juice is \(0.10m\) pounds.
Adding the contributions gives \(0.15o+0.10m=18\), choice B.

latihan.question: A lab mixes Solution A, which is 8% salt, and Solution B, which is 25% salt. The lab needs 60 liters of a solution that is 17% salt. If \(x\) and \(y\) are the numbers of liters of Solutions A and B, which system models the situation?
discussion: The total volume is 60 liters, so \(x+y=60\).
The final solution contains \(0.17(60)=10.2\) liters of salt.
The salt contributions are \(0.08x\) and \(0.25y\), giving the system in choice A.

latihan.question: A bookstore ships \(n\) boxes of novels and \(t\) boxes of textbooks. Each novel box weighs 14 pounds and costs USD \(18\) to ship. Each textbook box weighs 22 pounds and costs USD \(26\) to ship. The shipment must weigh no more than 520 pounds, cost no more than USD \(620\), and have at least one textbook box for every three novel boxes. Which system models the situation?
discussion: The weight limit gives \(14n+22t\le520\).
The shipping-cost limit gives \(18n+26t\le620\).
“At least one textbook box for every three novel boxes” means \(t\ge\frac13n\).
All three conditions appear in choice A.

latihan.question: A delivery app charges a USD \(12\) booking fee and USD \(2.40\) per mile. After the subtotal is calculated, the city adds a 5% surcharge to the entire amount. If \(m\) is the number of miles, which expression represents the total cost?
discussion: The subtotal is the fixed fee plus the mileage charge: \(12+2.4m\).
A 5% surcharge makes the total 105% of the subtotal, so multiply by \(1.05\).
The total cost is \(1.05(12+2.4m)\), choice A.

additionalPractice.question: A notebook costs USD \(4\). Which expression represents the cost of \(n\) notebooks?
discussion: The cost is USD 4 for each notebook.
For \(n\) notebooks, multiply 4 by \(n\): \(4n\).
Therefore, choice B is correct.

additionalPractice.question: Leo is 5 years older than Ana, whose age is \(a\). Which expression represents Leo's age?
discussion: “5 years older than Ana” means add 5 to Ana's age.
Leo's age is \(a+5\), so choice C is correct.

additionalPractice.question: The number of red cards in a collection is 4 fewer than twice the number of blue cards. If \(r\) is the number of red cards and \(b\) is the number of blue cards, which equation represents the relationship?
discussion: Twice the number of blue cards is \(2b\).
Four fewer than \(2b\) is \(2b-4\).
Thus, \(r=2b-4\), choice A.

additionalPractice.question: A music service charges a fixed fee of USD \(7\) plus USD \(2\) per downloaded album. Which equation represents the total cost \(C\) for \(a\) albums?
discussion: The per-album charge is \(2a\).
The fixed fee is 7, so it is added to the variable charge.
Therefore, \(C=2a+7\), choice B.

additionalPractice.question: A school admits \(m\) students in the morning and twice as many in the afternoon. If the total is 96 students, which equation can be used to find \(m\)?
discussion: The morning group has \(m\) students.
The afternoon group has twice as many, or \(2m\) students.
Adding both groups gives \(m+2m=96\), choice C.

additionalPractice.question: A quantity is increased by 40% and then decreased by 25%. If the original quantity is \(q\), which expression represents the final quantity?
discussion: Increasing by 40% multiplies the original by \(1.40\).
Decreasing the new value by 25% multiplies it by \(0.75\).
The final value is \(q(1.40)(0.75)\), choice B.

additionalPractice.question: A theater sells adult tickets for USD \(14\) and student tickets for USD \(9\). If \(x\) adult tickets and \(y\) student tickets are sold, write an expression for the revenue and an equation if exactly 80 tickets are sold.
discussion: Adult-ticket revenue is \(14x\), and student-ticket revenue is \(9y\).
Adding the two sources gives \(R=14x+9y\).
Exactly 80 tickets means the ticket counts add to 80, so \(x+y=80\).

additionalPractice.question: A school has \(x\) ninth-grade students and \(y\) tenth-grade students. There are 24 more tenth-grade students than ninth-grade students, and there are 416 students in total. Write a system of equations.
discussion: “24 more tenth-grade students” translates to \(y=x+24\).
The total enrollment is \(x+y=416\).
Together, these equations form the required system.

additionalPractice.question: A school can accept no more than 1,200 students and must reserve at least 100 places for transfer students. If \(b\), \(g\), and \(t\) represent boys, girls, and transfer students, write a system of inequalities.
discussion: The total number of students is \(b+g+t\).
“No more than 1,200” gives \(b+g+t\le1200\).
“At least 100 transfer students” gives \(t\ge100\).
